verdict: Altria raised cigarette prices again and it worked: revenue rose 1% to $6.1B despite shipping 4% fewer cigarettes, and profit rose 6% to $2.5B, helped by a $242M gain on its Anheuser-Busch stake.

kpis.label: Smokeable operating margin
kpis.note: adjusted OCI margin — pricing power in a shrinking market

segments.name: Smokeable products
segments.note: Cigarettes (Marlboro above all) and large cigars. Pricing rose; shipment volume fell about 4% after adjusting for trade inventory movements, and discount brands took a bigger share.

segments.name: Oral tobacco products
segments.note: Moist snuff (Copenhagen, Skoal) and on! nicotine pouches — flat, as pouch growth offsets declining snuff volumes.

segments.name: All other
segments.note: NJOY e-vapor, Horizon and other new-platform activities — still tiny and mostly research spending.

opex.name: Marketing, administration and research
opex.note: Marketing brands like Marlboro, running the company and researching reduced-risk products.

opex.name: General corporate expenses
opex.note: Head-office costs not charged to the segments.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: Write-down of brands and assets bought in past deals.

otherDetail: Interest and other debt expense of $270M, partly offset by a $242M gain on equity investments (mainly its stake in brewer Anheuser-Busch InBev) and $5M of pension benefit income.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding. Altria keeps about $41 of every $100 it takes in.

takeaways.title: Fewer cigarettes, more money
takeaways.text: Domestic cigarette shipment volume fell about 4%, but higher prices more than covered it — smokeable revenue rose 0.8% and segment operating income rose 3.8%.

takeaways.title: The beer stake chipped in
takeaways.text: Altria booked a $242M gain on equity investments, mainly its holding in Anheuser-Busch InBev — a meaningful slice of the quarter's 6% profit growth.

takeaways.title: An extraordinary margin
takeaways.text: The smokeable segment converts about 65 cents of every net-of-tax revenue dollar into operating income — the economics that fund Altria's dividend even as volumes shrink.

footerNote: Altria's 'cost of revenue' here combines $1,500M of cost of sales with $691M of excise taxes on products — taxes Altria collects in the price of a pack and passes to governments. Net earnings attributable to Altria were $2,518M; consolidated net earnings were $2,514M because a noncontrolling interest absorbed a $4M loss.
